summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes and bilateral below-knee amputations was admitted for fever and pyuria. She had a history of multidrug-resistant UTIs and recent sepsis. On admission, she had leukocytosis, acute kidney injury, and cellulitis of the left stump. Urine culture grew ciprofloxacin-resistant E. coli, and tissue cultures from a stump revision grew ESBL-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae and E. coli. An MRI was inconclusive for osteomyelitis, but due to clinical concern, she underwent stump revision and was started on IV tigecycline. Her kidney function improved with fluids, and she completed a course of vancomycin for soft tissue infection. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic therapy. She was discharged home on a six-week course of IV tigecycline with follow-up in Infectious Disease, Vascular Surgery, and primary care.
